note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer with a history of hyperthyroidism, presenting with new intermittent frontal headaches, palpitations, tingling in both hands, unintentional weight loss, decreased appetite and libido, beginning after a recent job change; clinical impression favors possible hyperthyroidism relapse/over-replacement or stress-related etiology.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Feeling intermittently hot, severe intermittent frontal headaches impacting work, palpitations (heart beating fast), tingling in both hands (not legs), reduced appetite with 5 lb unintentional weight loss, occasional shortness of breath at rest, and reduced libido.
- Symptom timeline: All symptoms began since changing jobs (legal sector, London); symptoms occur at separate times, not all at once; most headaches occur during work (meetings/computer use), palpitations mainly in mornings, tingling noted recently and only in hands.
- Associated symptoms: Mild nausea with headaches; no visual changes, diarrhea, tremors, or worsening with exercise; no similar prior episodes.
- Pertinent negatives: No lower limb tingling, no weight loss noticed by others, no significant exercise intolerance; no drug use, no smoking.
- Past medical history: Hyperthyroidism.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Medications: Thyroxine, taken regularly.
- Social/preventive: Lawyer; increased work-related stress (7–8/10); drinks alcohol socially (~2 glasses wine/week); no smoking or recreational drug use.

Examination:
- No physical/vital findings available (teleconsultation only).
- No observed tremor, eye signs, or abnormal neurological findings reported.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: 
  - Hyperthyroidism relapse or over-replacement (most likely, per DDx and transcript: history of disease, current thyroxine use, symptoms of palpitations, weight loss, appetite/sexual changes, intermittent hot feelings, headaches).
  - Stress/anxiety-related somatic symptoms (supported by increased work stress, temporal association with job change, multiple somatic complaints).
  - Migraine (less likely, but considered due to severe frontal headaches with mild nausea and possible tingling in context of new job).
- Pituitary or other intracranial pathology: Low likelihood at present but flagged due to combined headache and libido loss (no focal neurology or visual changes).

Plan:
- In-person clinical examination to assess cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological systems.
- Blood tests to check thyroid function (thyroxine levels and related markers).
- Consider further investigations or referrals depending on examination and lab results.
- No new medication started prior to in-person assessment.
- Patient advised on appointment process and reassured that history will be shared with clinic.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements: Objective examination findings and vital signs (planned for in-person visit); review of recent thyroid function tests; follow-up arrangements after labs and exam; additional review of other possible causes (e.g., migraine triggers, pituitary symptoms) if relevant.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted; transcript facts consistent with leading DDx.
● Transcript quality: Reasonably complete for telehealth; moderately fragmented but covers relevant history, review of systems, and basic functional/social risk factors; physical exam and objective findings not available due to remote format.
